newsitem.title: BRAZIL: OLYMPICS-HAVELANGE PROMISES RIO WILL BE ON 2004 SHORTLIST.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-HAVELANGE PROMISES RIO WILL BE ON 2004 SHORTLIST.

text.p: FIFA boss Joao Havelange, who caused a storm in January by pledging the 2006 World Cup to Africa, has revealed that Rio de Janeiro will be on the shortlist to host the 2004 Olympics.

"Rio will be among the five cities selected for the final stage of the choice for the 2004 Olympics," the president of international soccer's governing body told the Rio de Janeiro daily newspaper O Globo on Thursday.
"I can tell you that its (the Rio 2004 committee) report was considered one of the best by the IOC," he added.
At the start of the year, Havelange caused uproar when he told another Brazilian paper he would promise South African president Nelson Mandela that Africa would host the 2006 World Cup.

"(African soccer) is the football of the future," he said at the time. "To reward the progress that has been made, I will tell president Nelson Mandela ... that the 2006 World Cup will be on their continent."
His attitude was condemned as authoritarian by Lennart Johansson, president of the European Football Union, UEFA.
"It's dictatorial. It's not for the president to travel around the world deciding where the World Cup should be held," Johansson said.
Havelange's latest remarks came on the day a group of IOC officials was due to arrive in Rio to begin their inspections of the city's facilities.
